title: Shared Build Services, Workers, and Parallel Safety Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies shared build services, workers, and parallel safety?
options: Expose independent work while controlling genuinely shared resources through lifecycle-managed services.
Let workers write one shared output file
questions.answer: Expose independent work while controlling genuinely shared resources through lifecycle-managed services.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: A BuildService automatically makes any hidden state part of a task cache key.
questions.explanation: Putting a mutable result cache inside a BuildService without modelling its inputs can make task output depend on invocation order and daemon history.

questions.prompt: When should process isolation be preferred for worker actions?
questions.answer: When work needs stronger process-state or classpath isolation than in-process or classloader-isolated execution provides.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
